full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: The accused-petitioner Mohashin Ali Pramanik now in jail custody in invoking this Court's Jurisdiction under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeks bail on setting aside the order dated 21-6-2000 recorded by learned Sessions Judge, Rajshahi in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 180 of 2000 cancelling bail of accused-petitioner which was granted by him by his order dated 2-5-2000. 

 2. Md. Golam Rabbani, Chairman of Shuvadanga Union Parishad, Rajshahi was murdered on 16-1-2000. Following murder law was set in motion on laying a First Information Report by Md Golam Rahman, brother of deceased Md Golarn Rabbani as informant which led to registration of Bagmara Police Station Case No. 10 dated 16-1-2000. In First Information Report in the list of accused persons the name of accused- petitioner does not appear but in the body of First Information Report he is made a suspect as he was found roaming about in the Bazar half an hour to occurrence. 

 5. Bail was sought before learned Magistrate but without any result. Bail was then moved before learned Sessions Judge, Rajshahi in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 139 of 2000. Learned Sessions Judge released accused-petitioner on bail by order dated 2-5-2000. Bail bond of the accused- petitioner was accepted 3-5-2000 and accused- petitioner was freed from jail custody on the said date i.e. 3-5-2000. 

 6. On 10-5-2000 after a period of only seven days of freedom of bail granted to accused-petitioner, informant presented an application being numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 180 of 2000 before learned Sessions Judge for cancellation of bail of accused-petitioner. Grounds pressed for cancellation of bail were that accused-petitioner having been enlarged on bail had been attempting to tamper with evidence and had been hampering the due process of investigation and truth would remain in dark and two GD Entries had been registered. Informant, wife of deceased, who is newly elected Chairman of Subudanga Union Parishad, and four other persons had been examined in support of grounds for cancellation of bail. 

 7. Learned Sessions Judge, Rajshahi by Order dated 21-6-2000 allowed Miscellaneous Case and cancelled bail granted to accused petitioner on 2-5-2000 and directed accused-petitioner to surrender to court below. In cancelling bail on allowing Miscellaneous Case Sessions Judge held that it stood proved that the accused-petitioner held meeting on 3-5-2000 and 6-5-2000 as alleged by prosecution and holding of public meeting might be termed as threat to prosecution witnesses and petitioner misused privilege of bail. 

 (ii) The case is under Investigation and investigating agencies did not put forward allegation that process of investigation was going to be hampered through tampering with witnesses and cause of justice was going to be interfered with. 

 10. Law and principles regulating cancellation of bail may be looked into. Under sub-section 5 of section 497 of The Code of Criminal Procedure High Court Division or Court of Session and in the case of a person released by itself any other Court may cause any person who has been released on bail to be arrested and may commit him to custody, The power to take back in custody an accused who has been enlarged on bail has to be exercised with care and circumspection. This power which is extraordinary in nature is meant to be exercised in appropriate cases when by a preponderance of probabilities it is manifestly clear that the accused is interfering with the course of justice by tampering with witnesses. 

 11. Rejection of bail when bail is applied for is one thing but cancellation of bail already granted is quite another thing. It is easier to reject a bail application in a non-bailable case than to cancel a bail granted in such a case. Cancellation of bail necessarily involves the review of a decision already made. and can by and large be permitted only if by reason of supervening circumstances. it would be no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom during trial. Generally, grounds for cancellation of bail broadly, are interference or attempt to interfere with due course of administration of justice or evasion or attempt to evade course of justice or abuse of liberty granted to him. The administration of justice may be interfered with by intimidating or suborning of witnesses or holding out threats or interfering with investigation or causing disappearance of evidence. 

 12. Proof of facts by preponderance of probabilities as in Civil Cases is not foreign to Criminal Jurisdiction. The same standard of proof as in a Civil Case applies to incidental issues involved in a Criminal trial like the cancellation of bail of an accused. BaiI can be, thus, cancelled on a proper application for cancellation of bail by showing a preponderance of probabilities that the accused has interfered with course of justice. Where accused allegedly threatened informant party with dire consequences but no untoward incident had taken place since his release on bail. bail granted to accused cannot be cancelled. 

 14. In First Information Report accused petitioner is not named in the list of accused persons and he was made a suspect therein. Learned Sessions Judge in granting bail by order dated 2-5-2000 took into account facts and circumstance of case and judicial confessional statements recorded under section 164 and also statements under section 161 of The Code of Criminal Procedure of other accused persons and held that no statements had been made involving accused-petitioner in occurrence. Sessions Judge, also, held that no cogent evidence had been collected for involvement of accused petitioner in commission of crime. Sessions Judge, also, found that enmity existed between deceased and accused petitioner over Union Parishad Election. 

 16. The case is under Investigation by investigating agencies. Investigating agencies did not put forward any allegation by way of application before learned Sessions Judge that investigation was being hampered and witnesses were attempted to be tampered and course of administration of justice was being interfered with. From Order dated 2-5-2000 recorded by Sessions Judge and materials on record it transpires that during investigation the statements of First Information Report named accused Faroque alias Fartul and other accused persons had been recorded under section 164 and section 161 of The Code. In the absence of any complaint from the side of investigating agency it is difficult to suggest that investigation was going to be hampered and course of administration of justice was interfered with. In application for cancellation of bail there had been no statements that accused petitioner on being released on bail held public meetings on 3-5-2000 at Hatganga para and 6-5- 2000 at Bujrok Kour School field wherein he threatened informant and wife of deceased to face dire consequences and untoward incident had taken place. Of course, witnesses who stood on witness box testified that accused petitioner declared in the meeting that informant, wife of deceased and witnesses would be finished and removed from the world. Learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail taking view that accused petitioner held meeting as alleged by prosecution and that holding of public meetings might be termed to be threat to prosecution witnesses. Learned Sessions Judge was not at all justified in taking into account the case of holding of public meetings where the alleged threat was given by accused-petitioner when no statement and no case had been made out in the application for cancellation of bail that the accused petitioner in two public meetings held on 3-5-2000 and 6-5-2000 declared before public to finish and remove informant, wife of deceased and other witnesses from the world. 

 18. The case set up by informant side that on getting bail on 3-5-2000 accused petitioner held a meeting and in meeting he threatened informant, wife of deceased and other witnesses stands in doubt in the light of probability and improbability. It is difficult to digest that an accused, here the accused petitioner, on getting freedom of bail on the very date i.e. on 3-5-2000, in open meeting would mount threat to finish and remove informant and other persons from world. The accused petitioner might be indulged in conspiracy to remove informant and wife of deceased and other witnesses but could not openly and publicly make declaration of finishing them from world. 

 20. This takes us to the contention raised from the side of State that the application for cancellation of bail at the instance of Informant was not tenable and only the State could move such an application for cancellation of bail. This contention cannot be accepted. True it is that in a case instituted on a Police Report State becomes prosecutor but following a commission of crime or incident, law is set in motion by a private party as Informant, ofcourse, sometimes Police personnel’s, also, figure as Informant when no private person comes forward and that happens under special and compelling circumstances. The real pain for the crime is with Informant and not with State as prosecutor. Ordinarily, State should make an application for cancellation of bail. But when a private party feels aggrieved in a proper case, he should not be prevented from making application for cancellation of bail. There cannot be any gainsaying that informant, in any view of the matter, is incompetent to move any application for cancellation of bail even if State does not move any application. But it is also to be borne in mind that informant can move for cancellation of bail on satisfaction of two factors: 

 a)	Order granting bail has occasioned a gross miscarriage of justice and wholly an abuse of process of court and 

 21. Before an order for cancellation of bail is recorded it is to be satisfied that granting of bail to accused person has occasioned a grave miscarriage of justice and an abuse of process of court and the alleged threat is real and not fanciful. 

 23. Section 498 of The Code empowers High Court Division and Court of Session to admit any person on bail and in any case whether there be an appeal on conviction or not. 

 25. Revisional Jurisdiction of High Court Division under section 439 of The Code of Criminal Procedure is a kind of Paternal and Supervisory Jurisdiction exercised to correct a miscarriage of justice arising from apparent harshness of treatment resulting in some injury and undeserved hardship to an individual. Revisional Jurisdiction of High Court Division is in its real purpose, not merely a power but a duty which is to be exercised in aid of justice. High Court Division may exercise Revisional Jurisdiction on the application of a party or even suo-moto, the words "which otherwise comes to its knowledge" means which comes to the knowledge of High Court Division in any other way. When any matter is brought before High Court Division in any case or proceeding which is incompetent, the case or the proceeding comes to the knowledge of High Court Division within the meaning of section 439 of the Code. Thus, whenever a matter is brought to the notice of High Court Division and High Court Division is satisfied that in the facts and circumstances of the case, a case is made out for exercising Revisional power suo-moto, it can always do so in the interest of justice and can treat an incompetent proceeding to be a proceeding under section 439 of The Code it is well recognised that the principal object behind all legal formalities is to safeguard paramount interest of justice and mere technicalities cannot be allowed to defeat justice. 

 26. In view of the above, in exercise of our power under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure we treat the petition under section 498 of The Code to be a petition under section 439 of the Code and convert Criminal Miscellaneous case into Criminal Revision Petition (case). 

 Resultantly, converted Criminal Revision Petition (case) is allowed. Rule issued on 5-11-2000 is made absolute. The order dated 21-6-2000 recorded by Learned Sessions Judge Rajshahi in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No 180 of 2000 cancelling bail to accused-petitioner stands set aside and the order dated 2-5-2000 granting bail to accused petitioner is restored. The accused petitioner is released on bail on the same bail bond furnished by him on 3-5-2000.
